description.p: Locus is a system monitor for Wayland desktops, built with GTK 4 and libadwaita. It graphs the whole machine, and lists the running apps and processes with what each takes of the processor, the memory and the disks.

ul.li: Processor usage as a whole and for each core, memory and swap, network and disk traffic, and the usage, video memory and temperature of each graphics card its driver reports
Room left on each mounted disk
Running apps with their processes, and every other process beneath the one that started it, sorted by processor, memory, disk or graphics card use and searchable by name, command line or ID
End, kill, stop and continue a process, or end an app with all its processes, from its menu or the buttons above the list

description.p: Everything is read from /proc and /sys, and processes are read only while their list is on screen.

screenshot.caption: Watch the processor, memory, network and disks over time
Follow each graphics card's usage, video memory and temperature
Find the apps and processes that keep the machine busy

description.p: Locus does much less work to stay open. Reading the processes costs a fraction of what it did, file systems are read only while their page is shown, and a hidden window no longer updates what nobody can see. The window fills in at once on launch, with the processor, network and disk figures following a moment later. Processes showing the same processor use keep their places instead of swapping on every update, and the process list holds less memory. A process that starts using a graphics card can take a few updates to show it in the GPU column.

The first release: running apps and processes with their processor, memory, disk and graphics card use, which can be ended, killed, stopped and continued; graphs of the processor, each of its cores, memory and swap, the network, the disks and the graphics cards; and the room left on each mounted disk.
